questions.text: The government's new initiative seeks to ______ the gap between digital literacy and employment opportunities in rural areas.
questions.solution: The phrase "bridge the gap" is a fixed idiom meaning to reduce or eliminate a disparity. While "fill", "close", and "reduce" can collocate with "gap", the standard expression in policy contexts is "bridge the gap". Hence the correct choice is "bridge".

questions.text: While the government's new scheme seeks to alleviate the financial strain on marginal farmers, it inadvertently ______ the administrative burden on state agencies.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the discourse marker "While" at the start – it signals a contrast between the two clauses.
2. The first clause uses "alleviate" (meaning to reduce or ease).
3. Because of the contrast, the second clause must express the opposite effect – an increase in burden.
4. Among the options, only "escalate" means to increase or intensify.
5. "Mitigate", "lessen", and "curtail" are synonyms of "alleviate" and would continue the same direction, violating the contrast.
6. Therefore the correct fill is "escalate".

questions.text:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows:

"The new railway safety protocol, introduced after a series of minor accidents, mandates that train operators must *eschew* any form of complacency during peak hours. Instead of relying on routine checks alone, they are required to *scrutinize* each signal with heightened vigilance, ensuring that no oversight compromises passenger safety. This proactive stance has been praised for its *efficacy* in reducing delays and accidents."

Which word from the passage is closest in meaning to the word "eschew" as used in the first sentence?

A) Embrace
B) Avoid
C) Encourage
D) Tolerate
questions.solution: The word "eschew" means to deliberately avoid or keep away from. Among the options, only "Avoid" matches this meaning. Hence option B is correct.

questions.text: Select the option that best completes the analogy: Cuboid : Volume :: Circle : ?
questions.solution: A cuboid is a 3‑dimensional figure measured by volume; a circle is a 2‑dimensional figure measured by area. The relationship is ‘3D shape : its measure :: 2D shape : its measure’. Hence Area is the answer.

questions.text: Find the next term in the series: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
questions.solution: The differences between consecutive terms are 3, 5, 7, 9 – consecutive odd numbers. The next difference is 11, so 26 + 11 = 37. Shortcut: check the pattern of differences; they increase by 2 each step.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FISH’ is written as ‘HKUJ’. How will ‘BIRD’ be written in that code?
questions.solution: Each letter in the word is shifted forward by two places in the alphabet (A→C, B→D, …). Applying the same rule to BIRD gives D K T F. Shortcut: identify the constant shift by comparing the first pair of letters.

questions.text: Pointing to a lady, a man said, ‘She is the daughter of the only son of my father’s wife.’ How is the lady related to the man?
questions.solution: The man’s father’s wife is his mother. The only son of his mother is the man himself (assuming he is the only son). The daughter of that son is the man’s daughter. Hence the lady is his daughter. Shortcut: break the statement step by step from the innermost relation.

questions.text: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution are the Fundamental Duties of citizens enshrined?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options related to Fundamental Rights first. Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) and Article 21 (Protection of Life and Personal Liberty) are Fundamental Rights (Part III). Article 51 deals with Directive Principles for international peace (Part IV). Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment in Part IV-A under Article 51A. Step-by-step: 1. Identify Part III (Rights) vs Part IV-A (Duties). 2. Discard Art 32 & 21. 3. Discard Art 51 (DPSP). 4. Select Art 51A.

questions.text: 'Majuli', recognized as the world's largest river island, is situated in which river?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use state-river mapping. Majuli is located in Assam. Among the options, only Brahmaputra flows through Assam. Ganga/Yamuna flow through North Indian plains; Godavari flows through Central/South India. Step-by-step: 1. Locate Majuli (Assam). 2. Identify major river in Assam (Brahmaputra). 3. Eliminate Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari based on geographical course. 4. Confirm Brahmaputra.

questions.text: Which Governor-General of India introduced the 'Doctrine of Lapse' policy?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Associate Governor-Generals with key policies. Lord Dalhousie (1848-56) is famous for annexation via Doctrine of Lapse. Lord Canning (1856-58) is linked to 1857 Revolt. Lord Cornwallis (1786-93) introduced Permanent Settlement. Lord Wellesley (1798-1805) introduced Subsidiary Alliance. Step-by-step: 1. Recall major annexation policy = Doctrine of Lapse. 2. Match with Dalhousie's tenure. 3. Verify others: Canning (Revolt), Cornwallis (Land Revenue), Wellesley (Subsidiary Alliance). 4. Select Lord Dalhousie.

questions.text: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Size comparison. Liver is the largest internal organ and gland (approx 1.5 kg). Pancreas is the second largest gland (mixed). Thyroid and Pituitary are small endocrine glands. Step-by-step: 1. Classify options: Liver (Accessory digestive/Metabolic), Pancreas (Mixed), Thyroid/Pituitary (Endocrine). 2. Recall Liver weight > Pancreas weight > Thyroid > Pituitary. 3. Select Liver as the largest gland.

questions.text: A and B together can complete a work in 12 days. B and C together can complete it in 15 days. C and A together can complete it in 20 days. In how many days can A alone complete the work?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Add the three pairwise rates: 1/12+1/15+1/20 = 1/5. Half of this gives combined rate of A+B+C = 1/10. Subtract B+C rate (1/15) to get A's rate = 1/10-1/15 = 1/30, so A alone takes 30 days. Full: Let a,b,c be daily work. a+b=1/12, b+c=1/15, c+a=1/20. Adding gives 2(a+b+c)=1/5 => a+b+c=1/10. Then a = (a+b+c)-(b+c)=1/10-1/15=1/30. Hence 30 days.

questions.text: If the numerator of a fraction is increased by 20% and the denominator is decreased by 10%, the fraction becomes 4/5. What was the original fraction?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The multiplier for numerator is 1.2, for denominator 0.9, so overall multiplier = 1.2/0.9 = 4/3. Since new fraction = 4/5, original = (4/5) ÷ (4/3) = 3/5. Full: Let fraction = x/y. (1.2x)/(0.9y)=4/5 => (4/3)(x/y)=4/5 => x/y = (4/5)*(3/4)=3/5.

questions.text: The perimeter of a rectangle is 60 cm and its length is twice its breadth. What is the area of the rectangle?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Length:breadth = 2:1, so perimeter 2(2x+x)=6x=60 => x=10. Breadth=10, length=20, area=200 cm². Full: Let breadth = b, length = 2b. Perimeter = 2(2b+b)=6b=60 => b=10, length=20. Area = 20×10 = 200 cm².

questions.text: What is the remainder when 7^95 is divided by 6?
questions.solution: Shortcut: 7 ≡ 1 (mod 6), so 7^95 ≡ 1^95 ≡ 1 (mod 6). Remainder = 1. Full: By modular arithmetic, 7 = 6+1, so 7^95 = (6+1)^95. All terms except 1^95 are multiples of 6, hence remainder 1.

questions.text: Choose the one word that best substitutes the phrase: 'A person who speaks many languages'.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options that do not imply speaking multiple languages – a linguist studies language, an orator is a public speaker, a rhetorician specializes in rhetoric. The term ‘polyglot’ directly means a person who knows and uses several languages. Full solution: ‘Polyglot’ derives from Greek ‘poly’ (many) + ‘glotta’ (tongue), precisely describing a multilingual person, whereas the other terms refer to language study, public speaking, or persuasive writing respectively.

questions.text: Select the meaning of the idiom ‘to burn the midnight oil’.

options.label: C
options.text: To work late into the night

questions.solution: Shortcut: Recall the historical context – before electric lights, people burned oil lamps at midnight to continue working; thus the idiom means working late. Eliminate ‘waste time’, ‘sleep early’, and ‘light a lamp’ as they do not convey extended work hours. Full solution: The phrase originates from the practice of using oil lamps for illumination during late-night study or labor, so it figuratively means to work or study late into the night.

questions.text: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: ‘She is married with a doctor since last year.’
questions.solution: Shortcut: The correct preposition after ‘married’ when indicating the spouse is ‘to’, not ‘with’; therefore the error lies in the second segment. Quick elimination: ‘She is married’ is grammatically sound, ‘since last year’ is a correct time expression, and ‘No error’ is false because the preposition is wrong. Full solution: In standard English, one says ‘married to someone’; ‘married with’ is used only when ‘with’ introduces an accompanying circumstance (e.g., ‘married with children’), not the spouse. Hence ‘with a doctor’ should be ‘to a doctor’.
